sections.h2: How can I sell my Haltom City house without repairs or showings?
sections.html:
Accept a cash offer for the house in its current state, or list it and fix whatever a financed buyer's inspector flags. Much of the housing dates from the postwar boom, so an as-is sale is a common choice for owners who do not want to put money into a house they are leaving.

The trade-off is price. A listing might bring a higher number along with repair requests, appraisal risk and a longer wait. Cash buyers trade a lower price for speed. Whoever you deal with, request the offer in writing with a closing date and a clear statement of who covers title charges.

  • Locate the deed, a payoff statement and the newest tax bill.
  • Write down known defects before anyone asks.
  • Note whether anyone is renting the house.

sections.h2: What is Haltom City and where does it sit in Tarrant County?
sections.html:
Haltom City is on U.S. Highway 377 about four miles northeast of Fort Worth in central Tarrant County. The Texas State Historical Association says the town was established around World War II, with about 200 people and two businesses in the late 1940s. Within roughly ten years 5,760 people lived there, and by the mid-1960s the count had soared to 32,100.

That fast, postwar growth means much of the housing dates from the mid-twentieth century, so ask a buyer or inspector early which systems need attention. The city also built a manufacturing base: in 1976 it had thirty-five factories making goods such as sheet-metal products, clothing, plastics and fiberglass, and sixty manufacturing plants by 1990. The population was 39,018 in 2000.

Because the city sits inside Tarrant County, a Haltom City owner deals with one county clerk and one appraisal district, which keeps paperwork simpler than in cities that straddle county lines.

sections.h2: Does Haltom City require a permit for short-term rentals?
sections.html:
Yes. The city says short-term rentals must register with the city to receive a permit and operate legally, and they must also remit hotel occupancy tax. The city defines a short-term rental stay as less than 30 consecutive days, and the occupant pays the tax while the owner or operator collects it and sends it in.

Haltom City hotel occupancy and short-term rental tax basics
ItemWhat the city states
Hotel occupancy tax rate7 percent
Stays coveredFewer than 30 consecutive days
Return and payment dueMonthly, by the last calendar day of the month after collection
Return needed with no revenueYes, a return is still required
PermitAnnual short-term rental permit application with the city

Source: City of Haltom City hotel occupancy and short-term rentals page.

The city uses an outside vendor to process the tax accounts, and its page lists a support line and email for login credentials. Short-term rentals are not offered any tax exemptions at this time, according to the same page. A house with a rental past should come with its permit and filing history for the buyer.

sections.h2: How does the Haltom City hotel tax process work step by step?
sections.html:
Short-term rental operators file monthly, even in a month with no bookings. The tax is due by the last calendar day of the month after collection, and penalties accrue after that. The city has contracted an outside firm to run the accounts, so new operators request login credentials from the support center by phone or email, then file and pay online, by phone or by mailed check.

Exemptions are narrow. The city lists permanent residents who stay at least thirty consecutive days, federal government business paid directly by the United States, and state government business paid directly by Texas, including public schools and political subdivisions. Nonprofits and charities are exempt from sales tax but not from this tax, and short-term rentals receive no exemptions.

The city also separates its own tax from sales tax: the state comptroller collects sales tax for the state, city and county, while the city collects hotel occupancy tax under its ordinances. Permit questions go to the planning and community development department at City Hall, which keeps Monday through Thursday hours and is closed the rest of the week.

sections.h2: Who sets the tax bill on a Haltom City house?
sections.html:
Appraisals and exemptions for Haltom City run through the Tarrant Appraisal District, which serves seventy-three taxing units countywide. Every unit sets its own rate from the district's values, and the district says exemption filings cost nothing.

The Comptroller's calendar fixes values on January 1, mails homestead notices around April 1, and closes rate adoption in late September, with bills following near October 1. A split-payment option lets an eligible owner pay half by November 30 and the remainder by June 30 of the following year.

Delinquency gets expensive fast. Starting February 1 the Comptroller lists a six percent penalty and one percent interest, with the penalty rising monthly until July 1, and an attorney fee may follow. Some collectors allow payment plans of up to 36 months on a residence homestead.

  • Keep paying the undisputed portion during any appraisal appeal.
  • The lien travels with the house, so the title company settles any unpaid year from your proceeds.
  • Request a current balance from the county tax office before signing.

sections.h2: Where do I look up and contest a Haltom City appraisal?
sections.html:
The Tarrant Appraisal District website offers a property search, a protest hearing search and an exemptions page. The district mailed its 2026 notices of appraised value in a new format, and it runs a legacy site and a new site side by side for different purposes, so follow the links on its home page rather than a saved bookmark. Haltom City properties sit in Tarrant County, so the same district also handles any exemption you file as a homeowner.

If you disagree with a value, file a protest within the window printed on your notice, and gather photos and repair estimates that document the condition of the house. Appeals that go past the appraisal review board lead to district court or arbitration, and the Comptroller advises owners to pay the undisputed tax in the meantime.

sections.h2: What relief is there for older, disabled or veteran owners in Haltom City?
sections.html:
Older and disabled homeowners get an added school exemption plus a school tax ceiling fixed at the level of the first qualifying year. According to the Comptroller, that ceiling can move proportionally to a new Texas homestead, and a surviving spouse of 55 or more may keep it.

Disabled veterans receive an exemption that scales with their rating, and a 100 percent rating supports a total exemption on a residence homestead. If you will buy again in Texas, ask the district how the ceiling would carry over before closing.

Homestead applications usually need to reach the district before May 1.

faqs.q: Does Haltom City charge hotel occupancy tax on short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The city states a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax on stays under 30 consecutive days, collected by the owner and sent to the city monthly.

faqs.q: Who appraises houses in Haltom City?
faqs.a: The Tarrant Appraisal District appraises property and handles exemptions for Haltom City and the other taxing units in the county.

faqs.q: What are the penalties if I miss my Haltom City property tax deadline?
faqs.a: Taxes unpaid on February 1 draw a six percent penalty and one percent interest, and the penalty rises monthly until July 1, according to the Comptroller.

faqs.q: Who must file a Haltom City hotel tax return?
faqs.a: Any hotel or short-term rental operator, monthly, even if the property earned nothing that month. Returns are due by the last day of the month after collection.

faqs.q: Is a nonprofit exempt from Haltom City hotel occupancy tax?
faqs.a: No. The city says only permanent residents of 30 days or more and certain federal and state government stays are exempt.
